name: Zircon-Void
description: Zircon-Void is a tiny, airless rock whose only distinction is the extraordinary concentration of zircon crystals embedded in its surface, remnants of the magmatic processes that formed it billions of years ago. The crystals are visible from orbit as a faint sparkle against the otherwise drab gray surface, and up close they range from colorless to pale brown, studding the impact-scarred terrain like frozen raindrops. Glass plains on the sunward face record an ancient thermal event that partially vitrified the surface.

With no atmosphere to soften the extremes, Zircon-Void alternates between searing heat and bone-cracking cold with each rotation. The solar wind has abraded the surface to a smooth finish in exposed areas, and the craters that pock every visible surface speak to a violent bombardment history. The silence is the vacuum silence of true void, absolute and unyielding.

Zircon-Void has no history beyond its formation. No civilization has touched it, no life has stirred on its surface, and no survey has found anything to justify more than a cursory scan. The zircon crystals are useful for radiometric dating of the system's formation but are otherwise unremarkable. The planet exists as a footnote in stellar cartography, a dot on a map that means nothing to anyone.

Occasionally, a research vessel will pause to collect zircon samples for chronometric analysis, and these brief visits constitute the entirety of Zircon-Void's recorded interaction with sapient beings. The planet asks for nothing and gives nothing, a mote of ancient stone turning slowly in the dark, perfect in its irrelevance.
